The Stark County Family Court is a court system in Ohio that focuses on family-related legal matters, including divorce, child custody, and child support. The court has a variety of resources available to help families navigate the legal system, and it works to ensure that the best interests of the children involved are always taken into account.

History of the Stark County Family Court

The Stark County Family Court was established in 1978 as part of a statewide initiative to create specialized courts that would focus on family-related legal matters. Prior to the creation of the Family Court, these cases were handled by the Stark County Court of Common Pleas.

Jurisdiction of the Stark County Family Court

The Stark County Family Court has jurisdiction over a wide range of family-related legal matters, including divorce, dissolution of marriage, legal separation, annulment, child custody, child support, and visitation rights. The court also handles cases involving domestic violence, juvenile delinquency, and adoption.

Divorce and Dissolution of Marriage

The Stark County Family Court handles both divorce and dissolution of marriage cases. In a divorce case, the court will decide issues related to the division of marital property, spousal support, and child custody and support. In a dissolution case, the parties work together to reach an agreement on these issues, and the court simply reviews and approves the agreement.

Child Custody and Support

Child custody and support cases are some of the most common types of cases handled by the Stark County Family Court. In these cases, the court will make a determination about which parent should have custody of the child, and it will also establish child support payments.

Domestic Violence

The Stark County Family Court also handles cases involving domestic violence. In these cases, the court will issue a protective order to protect the victim and any children involved.

Resources Available through the Stark County Family Court

The Stark County Family Court has a variety of resources available to help families navigate the legal system. These resources include:

Mediation

Mediation is a process in which a neutral third party helps the parties involved in a dispute to reach a mutually acceptable agreement. The Stark County Family Court offers mediation services to help families resolve their disputes outside of court.

Parenting Coordination

Parenting coordination is a process in which a neutral third party helps parents who are having disputes about child custody or visitation to come up with a parenting plan that is in the best interests of the child. The Stark County Family Court offers parenting coordination services to families who are in need of this type of assistance.

Self-Help Center

The Stark County Family Court has a self-help center that is designed to provide assistance to individuals who are representing themselves in court. The self-help center provides resources and assistance with filling out forms, understanding court procedures, and other legal matters.

Stark County Family Court Case Search

To look up information about a case that has been filed in the Stark County Family Court, individuals can use the online case search tool provided by the court. This tool allows users to search for case information by case number, party name, or attorney name. It provides access to a variety of information related to the case, including case details, case participants, case filings, and case events. By using this tool, individuals can stay up to date with the latest information about their case or the cases of others.

Stark County Family Court Filing Fees

When filing a case in the Stark County Family Court, individuals will need to pay certain filing fees. The amount of the filing fees will vary depending on the type of case being filed. For example, the filing fee for a divorce case is currently $300. Other fees that may be required include fees for copies, transcripts, and service of process. It is important to check with the court to determine the specific fees that apply to a particular case.

Stark County Family Court Clerk

The Stark County Family Court Clerk is responsible for a variety of duties related to the administration of the court. Some of the duties of the clerk include maintaining court records, issuing process and writs, administering oaths and affirmations, and accepting filings and fees. The clerk also provides assistance to individuals who are representing themselves in court and can help answer questions about court procedures and forms.

Stark County Family Court Forms

To file a case in the Stark County Family Court, individuals will need to use certain forms. These forms can be found on the court's website or obtained from the court clerk. Some of the forms that may be required include forms for filing a divorce, a motion, or a complaint for child support. It is important to use the correct forms and to fill them out completely and accurately to ensure that the case is processed correctly.

Stark County Family Court Local Rules

The Stark County Family Court has established local rules that govern the procedures and processes that are used in the court. These rules cover a variety of topics, including court filings, service of process, motions, discovery, and pretrial conferences. It is important for individuals who are involved in a case in the Stark County Family Court to be familiar with these rules to ensure that their case is processed correctly.

Stark County Divorce Court Docket

The Stark County Divorce Court Docket is a calendar of divorce cases that are scheduled to be heard by the court on a particular day. It provides information about the time and location of the court hearing, as well as the parties involved in the case and the issues that will be addressed. By consulting the docket, individuals can stay informed about when their divorce case is scheduled to be heard and can prepare accordingly.

Conclusion

The Stark County Family Court is an important resource for families in Ohio who are dealing with family-related legal matters. The court has a wide range of resources available to help families navigate the legal system, and it works to ensure that the best interests of the children involved are always taken into account.

FAQs

  1. How do I file for divorce in Stark County?

To file for divorce in Stark County, you need to fill out the appropriate forms and submit them to the Stark County Family Court. The forms can be obtained from the court or online, and you will need to provide information about your marriage, your spouse, and any children involved. You will also need to pay a filing fee.

  1. What is the process for establishing child support in Stark County?

To establish child support in Stark County, you will need to file a motion with the Stark County Family Court. The court will review your case and make a determination about how much child support should be paid. The amount of child support is based on a variety of factors, including the income of both parents, the number of children involved, and the needs of the children.

  1. Can I represent myself in court?

Yes, you can represent yourself in court, but it is generally not recommended. The legal system can be complex, and it is often helpful to have an attorney who can provide guidance and support. However, if you choose to represent yourself, the Stark County Family Court has a self-help center that can provide assistance with filling out forms and understanding court procedures.

  1. What is parenting coordination?

Parenting coordination is a process in which a neutral third party helps parents who are having disputes about child custody or visitation to come up with a parenting plan that is in the best interests of the child. The parenting coordinator works with both parents to identify areas of agreement and develop a plan that takes into account the needs of the child.

  1. What should I do if I am a victim of domestic violence?

If you are a victim of domestic violence, it is important to seek help right away. You can contact the police or a domestic violence hotline for assistance. The Stark County Family Court also has resources available to help victims of domestic violence, including protective orders and other forms of legal protection.
